summary: Today’s pulse tracks Democratic party infighting engulfs center-right over House rules vote, Andy Burnham pressed on borrowing costs and spending at first PMQs – UK politics live, and Hakeem Jeffries vows ‘serious response’ after two House Democrats vote with Republicans – US politics live. Across Guardian, Ars Technica, and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are party, house, and court. In the background, US court rules Google will not have to sell ad exchange after losing antitrust case and Woman charged with juror intimidation in Lindsay Clancy trial keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Democratic party infighting engulfs center-right over House rules vote
headlines.description: While leaders focused on Hasan Piker, two of the party’s more conservative members salvaged a GOP measure that was poised to fail House Democratic leaders have spent the past few weeks waging a bitter campaign against their own left flank over a leftwing streamer. On Tuesday, it was the party’s center-right who blindsided them. Hakeem Jeffries, the House minority leader, announced late on Tuesday that he had asked the Democratic caucus’s committee on caucus rules to consider punishing the retiring Jared Golden of Maine and Blue Dog Coalition leader Marie Gluesenkamp Perez of Washington after the pair sided with Republicans on a procedural vote that had appeared doomed.

headlines.title: Andy Burnham pressed on borrowing costs and spending at first PMQs – UK politics live
headlines.description: Burnham faced questions from Kemi Badenoch and other MPs amid speculation over budget In the news release to mark the first anniversary of his election as the Green party’s leader, Zack Polanski highlighted what he described as 10 achievements during his first year in charge. For the record, this is how he sees his record. -Won the Greens’ first ever parliamentary byelection in Gorton and Denton -More than tripled the party membership from 68,500 to over 230,000 Zack Polanski in Holborn and St Pancras sounds like a done deal from the hints the party is dropping over the past 24 hours. Needs the formality of local party sign-off. Our budget for day-to-day spending next year will be lower in real terms than this year. Our capital budget will fall in real terms every year until the end of the decade.

headlines.title: Hakeem Jeffries vows ‘serious response’ after two House Democrats vote with Republicans – US politics live
headlines.description: House minority leader says decision by two Democrats to advance resolution condemning socialism ‘represents significant breach of trust’ “We have hundreds of happy construction workers in D.C. busily doing their job building the finest Ballroom/Military complex anywhere in the World,” Trump said in a truth social post Wednesday morning. “There is nothing like it, and never will be! It was a long, hard, fight in the Court System, but the winner is, as always under ‘TRUMP,’ the U.S.A.”

headlines.title: US court rules Google will not have to sell ad exchange after losing antitrust case
headlines.description: The DOJ proved to the court that Google acted illegally, but it won't get the big win it wanted.

headlines.title: Woman charged with juror intimidation in Lindsay Clancy trial
headlines.description: Dawn Light is accused of taking photos of jurors outside the Plymouth courthouse, a practice prohibited by the court.

headlines.description: Chinese and Gulf state airlines are among those still using Russian airspace. Meanwhile, Russia says it will intensify its own attacks on Ukraine.

headlinePool.title: Understanding the tech giants' oversized influence in American schools
headlinePool.description: Big tech companies like Apple and Microsoft use devices, training and conferences for teachers and students to embed in schools. The New York Times' Natasha Singer discusses the impact in Coding Kids.

headlinePool.title: Rupert Murdoch ‘very happy’ that Guy Pearce plays him in Fleet Street biopic Ink
headlinePool.description: Actor says the press baron’s daughter Elisabeth told him her father was pleased, ‘but he hadn’t seen the film at that point’ Rupert Murdoch is “very happy” that he’s being portrayed by Guy Pearce in a new film about the origins of British tabloid the Sun, the Australian actor has said. Speaking at the Venice film festival ahead of the premiere of 28 Days Later director Danny Boyle’s Ink, Pearce said he had been messaging with the media tycoon’s daughter Elisabeth “and she did say ‘Dad’s very happy that you’re playing him’.”

headlinePool.title: Nepal intensifies relief and recovery efforts after deadly floods, UN says
headlinePool.description: More than 1,200 people have died and thousands are missing, as rescue efforts continue and aid is airlifted to villages.

headlinePool.title: Reform UK bans three journalists who have investigated party from its conference
headlinePool.description: Guardian City editor Anna Isaac, investigative reporter Peter Geoghegan and broadcaster Michael Crick refused entry Reform UK has banned at least three journalists who have investigated the party and Nigel Farage from its annual conference, which begins on Thursday. The Guardian’s City editor, Anna Isaac, the investigative reporter Peter Geoghegan and the broadcaster and biographer Michael Crick were told this week that their credentials to cover the event had been declined.

headlinePool.title: Russian airspace becoming unsafe for commercial airlines, Zelenskyy says
headlinePool.description: Ukraine president says aviation industry needs to take account of growing number of Ukrainian drones in Russia Europe live – latest updates Volodymyr Zelenskyy has declared that Russia’s airspace is becoming unsafe for commercial airlines as Vladimir Putin promised to step up strikes against Ukraine’s energy facilities in the run-up to winter. The Ukrainian president said there was no intention to directly threaten civilian flights, but the growing number of attack drones being flown into Russia by Ukraine would have to be “taken into account” by the aviation industry.

headlinePool.title: Russian ‘attempts to intimidate Europe will fail’, says EU’s Kallas as Germany blames Moscow for Leipzig drone incident – as it happened
headlinePool.description: EU’s policy chief says drone incident at German airport ‘had the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism’ German police have opened a investigation into yesterday’s attempt to disrupt the operation of a power substation near Brandenburg. In a statement , Brandenburg police said they were leading a probe on suspicion of attempting to disrupt public services, causing an explosion and damaging critical infrastructure as well as forming a terrorist organisation

headlinePool.title: Baby stabbed to death in Sheffield was found on top of washing machine, court told
headlinePool.description: Two men and two women charged with murder after body of newborn girl found with 33 stab wounds A newborn baby girl died from multiple stab wounds before she was found on top of a washing machine in an outhouse in Sheffield, a court has heard. Two men and two women appeared in court on Wednesday charged with the murder of the newborn, named only as Baby S. She was found with 33 wounds from 15 separate stabbings when police were called to a property in the Wincobank area of the city on Sunday.

headlinePool.title: Uber drivers launch European class action over ‘soulless’ and ‘scary’ AI algorithm
headlinePool.description: Landmark lawsuit claims tech company’s pay-setting system has breached privacy laws and pushed down earnings Uber drivers have launched a landmark legal action against the ride-hailing company claiming they live in “constant fear” of a “soulless” algorithm it uses to set pay and allocate jobs. Drivers from the UK, the Netherlands and other countries have joined the compensation claim that could run into billions of dollars. It alleges an AI-powered pay-setting system breaches data protection laws and pushes down their earnings.

headlinePool.title: Iran says US strike killed four at wedding in 'war crime' as US denies targeting civilians
headlinePool.description: Iranian media reports two children were among those killed when shrapnel hit a home. Iran then launched missiles and drones at US targets in the Middle East.
